see-commands: Run 'spec-controller --help' to see the commands this version accepts.
see-flags: Run ''{scope} --help' to see the flags this version accepts.
see-flags-and-values: Run ''{scope} --help' to see the flags this version accepts and the values they take.
see-arguments: Run ''{scope} --help' to see what this version accepts.
flag-before-command: The {flag} flag was given before the command. A command's own flags go after it, as in 'spec-controller <command> {flag}''.
missing-value: The {flag} flag of ''{scope}'' needs a value — {flag} {arg} — and was given none.
given-twice: The {flag} flag of ''{scope}'' was given more than once, and is read once: give it once.
equals-form: The {token} form is not read by ''{scope}'': a flag and its value are two arguments, as in ''{spelling}''.
takes-no-value: The {flag} flag of ''{scope}'' takes no value, and was given one: ''{value}''.
extra-argument: The argument ''{token}'' is more than ''{scope}'' takes: it takes {takes} once, and its flags.
not-a-flag: The argument ''{token}'' is not a flag, nor the value of the flag before it: ''{scope}'' takes only flags and their values.
unknown-flag: Unknown flag {flag} for ''{scope}'' — this is spec-controller {toolVersion}, and that flag is not in its {command} scope.
pin-drifted: If this version is pinned, the pin and the tree it is reading have drifted apart: bump the pin to a version whose ''{command}'' accepts {flag}.
otherwise-see-flags: Otherwise run ''{scope} --help' to see the flags this version accepts.
unknown-format: Unknown --format {formats}. Supported formats are {supported} (e.g. --format md, --format json:report.json).
more-than-one-to-stdout: More than one output routes to stdout ({formats}); at most one may. Give one of them a :<path> to write it to a file instead (e.g. --format json:report.json).
outputs-share-file: Two outputs name the same file: {first} and {second}. Give each output a file of its own.
output-overwrites-input: An output would overwrite a file this run reads: {output} is {subject}, {path}. Give the report a file of its own.
unknown-part-refused:
unknown part — no feature file's header carries {part}.
The parts this corpus's feature files carry: {parts}.
no-feature-part-given: no feature part was given: 'spec-controller allocate <FFF>' takes one, a feature file's header code.
not-a-feature-part: ''{part}'' is not a feature part: two to five characters, each A-Z or 0-9.
default-corpus-feature-file: a feature file of the corpus read by default
flagged-corpus-feature-file: a feature file of the --features corpus
default-ci-workflow: a CI workflow read by default
feature-corpus-directory-missing: The feature corpus directory does not exist: {directory}
default-feature-corpus: The feature corpus read by default
default-ci-workflows: The CI workflows read by default
junit-report-shape: of the JUnit XML report pytest --junitxml writes
jest-report-shape: of the JSON report jest --json writes
rspec-report-shape: of the JSON report rspec --format json writes
ci-step-record-shape: of a CI run's record of its steps
not-valid-json-in-shape: {subject} is not valid JSON, so not in the shape {shape}: {path} ({reason})
not-valid-xml: {subject} is not valid XML, so not in the shape {shape}: {path} ({reason})
corpus-file-unparseable:
{corpus} contains a feature file that could not be parsed: {file}
{message}
workflow-not-yaml:
{workflows} contain a workflow that is not valid YAML: {file}
{message}
report-not-written: The {format} report could not be written: {path} ({reason})
unexpected-error: spec-controller stopped on an unexpected error [unexpected-error], and gives no verdict: {name}: {firstLine}
unexpected-error-after-verdict: spec-controller hit an unexpected error [unexpected-error-after-verdict] after its verdict: {name}: {firstLine}
help-title: spec-controller — reconcile scenarios against observed evidence
help-pointer: Full flags, examples, and CI wiring: docs/user-guide.md.
balance-summary: Reconcile Gherkin scenarios against test/CI evidence and emit the Evidence Reconciliation (Markdown to stdout by default).
features-flag: Directory of Gherkin .feature files — the scenarios, and the `@`-tags naming what each must prove (@unit, @integration, @fitness, …).
vitest-flag: A Vitest JSON report — runtime test evidence.
pytest-flag: A pytest JUnit XML report (pytest --junitxml) — runtime unit test evidence.
jest-flag: A Jest JSON report (jest --json --outputFile) — runtime unit test evidence.
junit-flag: A JUnit XML report from any test runner that writes one, such as gotestsum --junitfile, or a directory of them, such as Maven Surefire's — runtime unit test evidence.
rspec-flag: An RSpec JSON report (rspec --format json --out) — runtime unit test evidence.
cucumber-flag: A Cucumber JSON report — runtime test evidence.
ci-flag: Your CI workflows — a file, or a directory of them (default .github/workflows). Where a fitness function you have not converted is found running over the real source, and where a check step's `id:` supplies the claim code its result cites.
package-json-flag: The target's package.json — its `scripts`, and its specController.runners, specController.notChecks and specController.deferralTags. A fitness function is named by its @fitness scenario and the CI step whose id: is that scenario's claim code; no manifest key names one.
ci-steps-flag: The CI run's own record of what each of its steps did — your pipeline's `toJSON(steps)` dump, evidence for the converted fitness functions. Omit it if you have converted none.
target-flag: A name recorded verbatim in the report's provenance (which project this run reconciled).
source-sha-flag: Override the git commit SHA recorded in provenance (defaults to the resolved HEAD).
format-flag: Where to send output (md or json, optionally :<path> to write to a file). Repeatable.
strict-flag: Read every scenario as if nothing were put off: a deferral tag is ignored, and a pending tag such as @integrationpending raises the Evidence Obligation it names.
exit-zero-flag: Print the same report but exit 0 on an out-of-balance (1) verdict — the on-ramp before gating. Usage (2), not reconciled (3) and an unexpected error (4) still fail.
allocate-summary: Print the next claim code for a feature part: one past the highest the repository has ever carried, the code alone on stdout.
feature-part-argument: The feature part: a feature file's header code, two to five of A-Z and 0-9.
new-flag: Start a part no feature file's header carries yet: its first code, or one past any number the repository already carries for it.
shallow-history-risks-part-code: history: shallow clone — history before {before} unread; a code of {part} may have been used before
shallow-history-risks-code-above: history: shallow clone — history before {before} unread; a code above {code} may have been used before
no-repository-risks-part-code: history: not a git repository — none read; a code of {part} may have been used before
no-repository-risks-code-above: history: not a git repository — none read; a code above {code} may have been used before
part-already-headed: note: a feature file's header already carries {part}, so --new was not needed
